Budget Discussion & Updates i. Current Status of Budget Adjustments – As discussed at the September 10th meeting, I have issued the budget cut memo to all departments, agencies and organizations who receive funding from the County directing a 5-10% cut. The range was added after realizing there are some areas where we can realize more than the originally proposed 5% (at this point, we need all the help we can get). We are working through a revised budget that would include corrections to the Revenues as well as the recommended Expenditure cuts. Since there are many conversations that still need to be held with the various agencies, I plan to present the revised budget in October for the Board’s review. ii. Davenport Recommendations – In addition, as previously reported, we have been working with Davenport and Company to assist with the analysis of the budget constraints and their recommendations, which will be incorporated into a revised budget. David Rose, Managing Principle at Davenport, is also working on a presentation that helps to summarize their review and recommendations and will provide it at the meeting. iii. Line of Credit Discussion – with the recent decision that the School Board’s Textbook fund is unavailable for use, we are likely to need to consider a larger amount of the line of credit, at a minimum in an amount that replaces the Textbook funds. The County Treasurer is recommending an increase from $5m to $10m and my recommendation would be a minimum of $7.5m. There is a slight likelihood that the line of credit will be needed in September but will almost certainly need needed in October with the large debt service payments related to the original Courthouse project as well as a school debt payment. Highway signage for the Visitor Center will also help draw travelers into Southampton and into the museum, where they can learn about the significant historical stories of Franklin and Southampton County, including the people and events — of both local and national importance -as well as of the forestry, agriculture, and manufacturing industries that helped shape the community. Community policy and management teams; membership; immunity from liability 9 17/2026 Code of Virginia Title 2.2. Administration of Government Chapter 52. Children's Services Act § 2.2-5205. Community policy and management teams; membership; immunity from liability. The community policy and management team to be appointed by the local governing body shall include, at a minimum, at feast one elected official or appointed official or his designee from the governing body of a locality that is a member of the team and the local agency heads or their designees of the following community agencies: community services board established pursuant to § 37.2-501, juvenile court services unit, department of health, department of social services, and local school division. The team shall also include a representative of a private organization or association of providers for children's or family services if such organizations or associations are located within the locality and a parent representative. Parent representatives who are employed by a public or private program that receives funds pursuant to this chapter or agencies represented on a community policy and management team may serve as a parent representative provided that parent representatives who are not employed by a public or private program that receives funds pursuant to this chapter or agencies represented on a community policy and management team are prioritized for participation where practicable. Those persons appointed to represent community agencies shall be authorized to make policy and funding decisions for their agencies. The local governing body may appoint other members to the team, including, but not limited to, a local government official, a local law-enforcement official, and representatives of other public agencies. When any combination of counties, citics or counties, and cities establishes a community policy and management team, the membership requirements previously set out shall be adhered to by the team as a whole. Persons who serve on the team shall be immune from any civil liability for decisions made about the appropriate services for a family or the proper placement or treatment of a child who comes before the team, unless it is proven that such person acted with malicious intent. Any person serving on such team who does not represent a public agency shall file a statement of economic interests as set out in § 2.2-3117 of the State and Local Government Conflict of Interests Act (§ 2.2-3100 et seq.). Persons representing public agencies shall file such statements if required to do so pursuant to the State and Local Government Conflict of Interests Act. Persons serving on the team who are parent representatives or who represent private organizations or associations of providers for children's or family services shall abstain from decision-making involving individual cases or agencies in which they have cither a personal interest, as defined in § 2.2-3101 of the State and Loca! Government Conflict of Interests Act, or a fiduciary interest. 1992. cc. 837. 880, § 2.1-751; 1995, c. 190; 1999, cc. 644, 669: 2001, c. 844; 2022, cc. 418, 419. https:/Haw.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title2.2/chapter52/section2.2-5205/ 1/1

text: SOUTHAMPTON COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS 7. Regular Session  September 22, 2026 Dams in Southampton County Ponds and Dams serve a vital function in Southampton County. Unlike many areas, we do not have fire hydrants and municipal water running to each household. Private ponds provide a means (in many cases the only means) to fight fires, give agricultural irrigation, and provide recreational activities in our 600 square mile rural community. title: Reimbursement Resolution
text: SOUTHAMPTON COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Regular Session * September 22, 2026 8. REIMBURSEMENT RESOLUTION - Project - TWO WELLS IN TURNER TRACT/BEALE FARM INDUSTRIAL PARK PROPERTY ! reached out to Davenport & Company, LLC to begin the process of financing the project of establishing two new wells that draw from the Potomac Aquifer. The wells will serve the industrial properties located on Rose Valley Road most commonly referred to as the Turner Tract and the Beale Farm areas (The Southampton Commerce and Logistics Park area) The amount included in the Capital Projects Plan is $3,860,000. We do not need all of the funds on hand at this moment in time, but the project has begun. Many of the up front items are not as capital intensive as later in the project. It will be best to pass a Reimbursement Resolution now so that we can capture all of the costs when the appropriate time comes to finance. The Reimbursement Resolution is attached. ACTION ITEMS: It is recommended that the Board approve the attached Reimbursement Resolution to allow project costs expended prior to financing to be reimbursed to the County when financing is obtained. A RESOLUTION DECLARING THE OFFICIAL INTENT OF THE COUNTY OF SOUTHAMPTON, VIRGINIA, TO REIMBURSE ITSELF FOR CERTAIN CAPITAL EXPENDITURES RELATED TO THE CONSTRUCTION OF CERTAIN PROJECTS WITH PROCEEDS OF DEBT A. The County of Southampton, Virginia (the "County"), intends (i) to acquire, construct, design, equip, replace, or renovate two wells on the Turner Tract and Beale Farm Industrial areas near Rose Valley Road (collectively, the "Project"), (ii) to pay costs of the Project from available funds of the County prior to the issuance or incurrence of bonds or other obligations or debt (the "Bonds") to finance the Project, and (iii) to reimburse itself for such original expenditures (the "Expenditures") from the proceeds of the Bonds. B. Bond counsel has advised the County that Treas. Regs. § 1.150-2 requires the County to adopt a resolution in the form set forth below to preserve the County's ability to use portions of the proceeds of the County's upcoming issues of Bonds to reimburse itself for the Expenditures. After careful consideration and to further the public purposes for which the County was created, NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE BOARD OF SUPERVISORS OF SOUTHAMPTON COUNTY, VIRGINIA, THAT: 1. The County intends to finance the Project through the issuance of one or more series of Bonds. The principal amount of the Bonds attributable to the Project is not expected to exceed $3,860,000. 2 This Resolution represents a declaration of "official intent" under Treas. Regs. § 1.150-2. 3: Prior to the issuance or incurrence of the Bonds, the County expects to pay the costs of the Project from its available funds. 4. On the date each Expenditure is paid, it will be a capital expenditure (or would be with a proper election) under general federal income tax principles or will otherwise comply with the requirements of Treas. Regs. § 1.150-2(d)(3). 5. The County reasonably expects to reimburse the Expenditures made prior to the issuance of the Bonds to finance the Project from the proceeds of the Bonds and the adoption of this Resolution is consistent with the budgetary and financial circumstances of the County. 6. This Resolution shall be in effect from and after its adoption. 227134642_2.docx CERTIFICATE OF SECRETARY The undersigned Secretary of the Board of Supervisors of Southampton County, Virginia (the "County"), hereby certifies that: 1. title: Request/Resolution for Traffic Study
text: SOUTHAMPTON COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Regular Session * September 22, 2026 9. TRAFFIC STUDY REQUEST/RESOLUTION - 58 ONTO GREEN PLAINS ROAD Calls have been received from citizens having safety concerns when turning from 58 onto Green Plains Road. This area is in William Hart Gillette’s Northwest District. A resolution is attached if the Board would like to send this concern on to VDOT and the Commonwealth Transportation Board for a traffic study. ACTION ITEMS: It is recommended the Board approve the attached resolution so that a traffic study can be completed along 58 where vehicles turn onto Green Plains Road. The Board of Supervisors of Southampton County, Virginia, in regular session on the 22nd day of September 2026, adopted the following: RESOLUTION WHEREAS, the Board of Supervisors (Board) has received numerous concerns from citizens regarding the overall safety of traffic turning onto Green Plains Road off Route 58; and WHEREAS, the Board believes the implementation of a turn lane off of Route 58 to Green Plains Road is a safety related improvement that would provide a safer environment for all people travelling; and WHEREAS, the Board is unaware of pending development that will significantly affect the existing traffic on these roads: and NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, the Board requests that VDOT conduct a safety study for a turn lane off Route 58 onto Green Plains Road in order to consider any and all safety improvements with the goal of improving the safety and welfare of its citizens and visitors to the County. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that a certified copy of this resolution be forwarded to the Virginia Department of Transportation Resident Engineer. Adopted on this 22"¢ day of September 2026. Mr. Schilling has been employed with the Town since March 2024. The Mayor and Council congratulated Mr. Schilling on his accomplishment. PUBLIC HEARINGS Special Use Permit – Rotary Club Mural at 37 Water Street - The application for review is a request for an artistic mural, exceeding sixty (60) square feet in size, on the north side of the building facing the intersection of N. Commerce Avenue and Manassas Street, located at 37 Water Street. Identiﬁed by Tax Map 20A8-6-C3. The property is zoned C-2, Downtown Business District. The Mayor opened the ﬂoor for the applicant to speak. Mr. Brett Hrbek spoke on behalf of the Rotary Club of Front Royal in support of Special Use Permit 260273 for the proposed Centennial Mural at 37 Water Street. Mr. Hrbek stated that the mural would commemorate the Rotary Club’s 100 years of service to the community and transform the highly visible north side of the building into a piece of public art. The mural was designed and will be painted by a local artist and Warren County High School art teacher. The artwork represents themes including peace, education, clean water, health, economic opportunity, environmental protection, and Rotary International’s eﬀorts to eradicate polio. Mr. Hrbek noted that the project is privately funded and will be installed on removable wood panels to allow for future repair, updates, or removal. A QR code is also proposed to provide information about the mural and its symbolism, with the intent of incorporating the mural into the Town’s public art and mural trail. Mayor Cockrell opened the Public Hearing. Kathy Wolfe- 431 Washington Avenue- Executive Director of Blue Ridge Opportunities and a Town resident, spoke in support of the proposed mural. Ms. Wolfe stated that Blue Ridge Opportunities is excited to partner with the Rotary Club to host the mural on its building and expressed appreciation for the opportunity to display a piece of artwork that reﬂects the positive nature of the organization and the individuals it serves. Ms. Wolfe noted that Blue Ridge Opportunities has had a longstanding relationship with the Rotary Club and has wanted a mural on the building for many years. No other speakers present, Mayor Cockrell, closed the Public Hearing. Councilman Ingram moved, seconded by Councilman Rappaport that Council approve the Special Use Permit for the Rotary Club mural, exceeding sixty (60) square feet, to be located on the north side of the building at 37 Water Street, identiﬁed as Tax Map 20A8-6-C3, in the C-2, Downtown Business District, as presented. Vote: Yes– Councilmembers Rappaport, DeDomenico-Payne, Ingram, Wood, Sealock, Vice Mayor Veitenthal No– None Absent–None Abstain– None ROLL CALL: Mayor Cockrell commended the Rotary Club for the proposed mural and expressed appreciation for the club’s contribution to the community. Council members also expressed support for the mural, noting its representation of Rotary’s commitment to community service, business leadership, and humanitarian eﬀorts. Discussion included the potential for the mural to enhance the area, future landscaping and seating opportunities near the mural, and coordination with the Town’s Public Works Department regarding existing trees in the area. Council also recognized the Rotary Club’s 100 years of service and its signiﬁcant local and international contributions. Special Use Permit – 508 Kendrick Lane- Junkyard- Special Use Permit-Council is requested to consider application submitted by Eagle Sky Industrial Park, LLC, to allow an Automobile Graveyard ("Junkyard") at 508 Kendrick Lane, identiﬁed by Tax Map Number 20A1-3-4. The property is zoned I-2, Industrial Employment District. Planning and Zoning Director Ms. Kopishke presented the request for a Special Use Permit to allow an Automobile Graveyard (“Junkyard”) at 508 Kendrick Lane. Ms. Kopishke stated that, at Council’s request, the application was reviewed by ACES in addition to Town staﬀ and the Planning Commission. ACES raised concerns regarding stormwater management and DEQ inspections, compliance with the Town’s Dark Sky lighting requirements, adequate screening and buﬀering, and vegetation removal. Ms. Kopishke noted that the applicant has an approved stormwater management plan through DEQ and that the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) would oversee the day-to-day operations of the automobile graveyard. She stated that any conditions imposed by Council should be related to mitigating impacts associated with the use, including stormwater runoﬀ and other environmental impacts. In response to Council questions, Ms. Kopishke stated that the property is currently an undeveloped ﬁeld, although other industrial uses and towing operations are in the surrounding area. She further explained that the applicant had previously amended the application to move the proposed use outside an area subject to certain covenants, after which the applicable federal agency declined further review. Ms. Kopishke conﬁrmed that the application did not include additional information regarding the applicant’s proposed operational procedures for the vehicles beyond the approved stormwater management plan Mayor Cockrell opened and closed the public hearing. Vote: Yes– Councilmembers Rappaport, DeDomenico-Payne, Ingram, Wood, Sealock, Vice Mayor Veitenthal No– None Absent–None Abstain– None ROLL CALL: PUBLIC COMMENTS NOT RELATED TO PUBLIC HEARINGS Jim Justice- 12 Chester Street, Town resident and business owner, spoke regarding concerns with the Town’s fencing regulations in the downtown historic district. Mr. Justice stated that a neighboring property owner constructed a fence approximately six feet from the front door of his building and that a dispute exists regarding whether the fence was constructed across the property boundary. He expressed concern that the current process places the burden and expense of resolving property-line disputes on the aﬀected property owner. Mr. Justice provided photographs illustrating fencing in the downtown commercial historic district and expressed concern that the current ordinance could result in excessive fencing that negatively impacts the character of the historic district. He requested that Council review the ordinance and consider whether it is being applied in a manner consistent with its intended purpose. REPORTS Report of Town Manager- Mr. Petty, reminded residents that Town Hall will be closed on Monday, September 7, for Labor Day, and that the next Town Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, September 8, at Town Hall. Mr. Petty recognized Andrew for his work at the Wastewater Treatment Plant and thanked Town staﬀ and members of the public who assisted during the summer storms. Report of Council Members Councilman Sealock reported attending the Good Lions ribbon cutting and noted that the event was well attended, with food vendors and trailers set up in the parking lot. He also reported that he will be attending a threat assessment training at Randolph-Macon Academy on Thursday and Friday. Councilman Wood congratulated Cars Changing Lives on giving away its 89th and 90th vehicles and noted that the organization is approaching its goal of 100 vehicles. He also announced an upcoming Murder Mystery Dinner fundraiser on September 24 at Shenandoah Valley Country Club, with proceeds beneﬁting Cars Changing Lives. Vice Mayor Veitenthal stated she has been occupied with August being back to school month. Councilman Rappaport reported attending the Reaching Out Now Gala in Winchester on August 2, which supports student mentorship, leadership experiences, and youth programming. He also attended the VML Finance Policy Committee meeting remotely on July 15, where topics included local audit costs, ASAP program funding, and HB 599 funding for local police departments. Councilman Rappaport also visited several local businesses on Main Street and Commerce Avenue. Lastly, he thanked the Energy Department for addressing the lighting issue on Kidd Lane. Report of the Mayor- Mayor Cockrell reported attending the Warren County Fair, the Hike Kidz Elementary Shopping Days, and the distribution of school supplies, clothing, and hygiene kits to local students. She also attended the Warren County Public Schools new teacher and staﬀ luncheon, National Night Out, and the Warren County Public Schools convocation. Mayor Cockrell announced the upcoming Young Life Golf Tournament on September 9th and Celebrate Kids Day, hosted by the Warren Coalition, on September 27th from 1:00 to 4:00 p.m. at the Health and Human Services Complex. She also noted that she will participate in the event’s pitch burst fundraiser to beneﬁt the Warren Coalition. Main Street- Council is requested to consider an appeal pursuant to Town Code §175-94 regarding the Board of Architectural Review’s(BAR) denial of a Certiﬁcate of Appropriateness for the replacement of 18 wood windows with vinyl windows at 501 E. Main Street. Staﬀ explained that the property is a contributing structure within the Historic District and that the vinyl windows were installed without prior BAR approval. The BAR previously denied the Certiﬁcate of Appropriateness and directed replacement of the windows with wood windows in accordance with the Historic District Design Guidelines. The applicant requested that Council overturn the BAR decision or allow the existing vinyl windows to remain, with an alternative request to replace only the front-facing windows. Ms. Kopishke presented the appeal and explained that the property is a contributing structure within the Historic District and that the vinyl windows had been installed without prior BAR approval. The BAR denied the Certiﬁcate of Appropriateness and directed that the windows be replaced with wood windows in accordance with the Historic District Design Guidelines. Ms. Kopishke reported that the applicant had also submitted applications for rehabilitation and reinstallation of the original wood shutters and for construction of a front porch. She explained that the shutters could be addressed administratively, while the proposed porch would require BAR review. Town Attorney Mr. Sonnett clariﬁed that the matter before Council was limited to the appeal of the BAR’s decision regarding the windows. The proposed shutters and porch were separate matters and could not be considered as part of the current appeal. The appellant’s representative, Ronald Baldwin, presented renderings of the proposed porch and discussed the historic appearance of the property. He stated that the property is currently used as apartments and that the porch would help restore its historic character. He also expressed the applicant’s preference to retain the existing vinyl windows, citing energy eﬃciency and environmental beneﬁts. Council discussed the scope of the appeal and the options available to Council pursuant to Town Code §175-94. MINUTES WYTHEVILLE TOWN COUNCIL MEETING MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 14, 2026 AT 6:00 PM MUNICIPAL BUILDING - 150 EAST MONROE STREET WYTHEVILLE, VA 24382 1. UNAPPROVED MINUTES RE: ATTENDANCE MEMBERS PRESENT: Vice-Mayor Candice Johnson, Councilwoman Cathy Pattison, Councilwoman Holly Atkins MEMBERS ABSENT: Mayor Beth Taylor, Councilman Joseph Hand, Jr. OTHERS PRESENT: Interim Town Manager Chris Slemp, Town Attorney Paul Cassell, Town Clerk Brandi Jones, Human Resources Director Laura Heldreth, Assistant Computer Operations Manager Jeff Hooper, Police Captain Kenny Akers, Police Corporal Kyle Counts, Police Officer Levi Rose, Randy Hamm, Mike Forrest, Lorraine Dunn, Justina Heath, Arthur Johnson, Janet Johnson, Kevin Fox 2. RE: CALL TO ORDER Vice-Mayor Johnson called the meeting to order. 3. RE: ESTABLISHMENT OF QUORUM Vice-Mayor Johnson established that a quorum of Council members was present. 4. RE: PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Councilwoman Atkins. 5. RE: APPROVAL OF AGENDA Vice-Mayor Johnson advised that the next agenda item is the Approval of Agenda. She inquired if there was a motion to approve the agenda. Motion made by Councilwoman Pattison, Seconded by Councilwoman Atkins. Vice-Mayor Johnson inquired if there was any discussion on the motion. There being none, the motion was approved with the following voting results, by roll call vote: Voting Yea: Councilwoman Pattison, Councilwoman Atkins, Vice-Mayor Johnson. 6. RE: 7:00 P.M. RECESS 6 Section 7, ItemA. Vice-Mayor Johnson advised that for informational purposes only, the agenda includes a 7:00 p.m. scheduled recess. 7. RE: CONSENT AGENDA A. RE: MINUTES OF THE REGULAR TOWN COUNCIL MEETING OF AUGUST 24, 2026 Vice-Mayor Johnson advised that the next agenda item is consideration by the Wytheville Town Council to approve the minutes of the regular meeting held on Monday, August 24, 2026. She inquired if there was a motion to approve the minutes as presented. Motion made by Councilwoman Atkins, Seconded by Councilwoman Pattison. ViceMayor Johnson inquired if there was any discussion on the motion. There being none, the motion was approved with the following voting in favor and there being no opposition: Voting Yea: Vice-Mayor Johnson, Councilwoman Pattison, Councilwoman Atkins. 8. RE: CITIZENS' PERIOD Vice-Mayor Johnson advised that the next agenda item is Citizens' Period. She stated that there were no citizens listed on the sign-in sheet who wished to address the Council during Citizens' Period. Vice-Mayor Johnson noted that if there were any citizens present who did not sign in on the sign-in sheet and they wished to address the Council during Citizens' Period, now would be the time to do so. There being none, she proceeded with the agenda. 9. RE: PRESENTATIONS TO TOWN COUNCIL A. RE: PROPOSED SPLASH PAD UPDATE Vice-Mayor Johnson advised that the next agenda item is a presentation by Interim Town Manager Chris Slemp regarding an update for the proposed splash pad. Interim Town Manager Slemp stated that the Town received a notice of award for a grant from the National Park Service, and he noted that the Town's portion will be $1.5 Million. He explained that $80,000 for that amount is for engineering work, architectural work, etc. Interim Town Manager Slemp advised that the Town will have to obtain the remainder of Withers Park from the County before it is eligible to receive the grant funds. He commented that he, Staff and Salt and Light representatives met with Carolina Recreation at the splash pad site to discuss design proposals, and that the designs should, hopefully, be received during the following week. Interim Town Manager Slemp continued to discuss the information that was reviewed with Carolina Recreation and additional grant funding for the splash pad in further detail. ViceMayor Johnson thanked Interim Town Manager Slemp for this information. B. RE: PROPOSED EMPLOYEE WELLNESS DAY Vice-Mayor Johnson advised that the next agenda item is a presentation by Director of Human Resources Laura Heldreth regarding a request to amend the Town's Personnel Ordinance to add a Wellness Day as an additional benefit for employees. 7 Section 7, ItemA. Director Heldreth stated that Councilwoman Atkins had requested that she research a Wellness Day for Town employees. She noted that she asked other localities how they addressed this topic. Director Heldreth remarked that several localities responded to her inquiry and advised that a majority of them did not have a policy addressing this topic. She commented that the localities who did address this topic do not have a separate policy for it, and that their sick leave policy has a day written into it for a "Wellness Day" or "Personal Day" that is included in the employee’s sick leave time. Director Heldreth advised that the Wellness Day could be a rest day, relaxation day, or activities that support overall physical and emotional wellness, etc. She stated that employees would not have to state the exact reason for being absent, other than requesting a wellness day or a personal day. Vice-Mayor Johnson inquired if there was any discussion regarding the information that Director Heldreth presented. She stated that she plans to reach out to Interim Town Manager Slemp regarding her opinions and thoughts on this topic. Vice-Mayor Johnson inquired of Director Heldreth regarding if an amendment would have to be made to the Town's current Personnel Policy. Director Heldreth stated that is correct, and that it would amend the Town's Sick Leave Policy to include the Wellness Day benefit. Councilwoman Atkins stated the following: "Ms. Heldreth, thank you for your research on that and your hard work. Do you mind I get a hard copy? I was trying to write them down. I know you said stress management day, blood work. If I can just come by, and maybe get a hard copy." Director Heldreth noted that she would put a hard copy of this information together for Councilwoman Atkins. The Council thanked Director Heldreth for her presentation. 10. RE: NEW BUSINESS A. RE: REQUEST FROM ITALIAN GARDEN CUISINE FOR A ONE-YEAR EXEMPTION FROM VIRGINIA CODE SECTION 10.1-1424.3. - EXPANDED POLYSTYRENE FOOD SERVICE CONTAINERS Vice-Mayor Johnson advised that the next agenda item is a Staff Report by Interim Town Manager Christopher Slemp regarding the request from Italian Garden Cuisine for a one-year exemption of Virginia Code Section 10.1-1424.3. - Expanded polystyrene food service containers prohibited; civil penalty, due to undo economic hardship (exemption will expire September 14, 2027). Interim Town Manager Slemp stated that this request is similar to the request that was recently approved from CJ's Pizza. He noted that the law allows the Town to grant a one-year exemption, and he commented that the Town would be allowed to approve one more exemption after this request. Interim Town Manager Slemp advised that Italian Garden Cuisine has demonstrated a financial hardship due to the law that bans styrofoam containers. He commented that Staff is still working with Town Attorney Cassell on a blanket exemption that would address these requests. Vice-Mayor Johnson inquired if the Council had any questions regarding this request. Councilwoman Atkins stated the following: "I do. Have you had anybody else reach out, or just Italian Garden?" Interim Town Manager Slemp stated that no other business has reached out to date. Councilwoman Atkins stated the following: "I know we had talked about maybe doing some, you know, publicizing and different things like that. Can you tell me where it's been publicized or who we've reached out to?" Interim Town Manager Slemp noted that the State had publicized through the Heath Department, however, the Town is waiting on a blanket exemption that is approved by the Town Council. Councilwoman 8 Section 7, ItemA. Atkins stated the following: "But just wondering. No one, nothing's been advertised?" Interim Town Manager Slemp explained that the Town is waiting to advertise this as a blanket exemption. There being no further discussion, Vice Mayor Johnson inquired if there was a motion to approve the request from Italian Garden Cuisine for a oneyear exemption of Virginia Code Section 10.1-1424.3. - Expanded polystyrene food service containers prohibited; civil penalty, due to undo economic hardship (exemption will expire September 14, 2027). Motion made by Councilwoman Pattison, Seconded by Councilwoman Atkins. ViceMayor Johnson inquired if there was any discussion on the motion. There being none, the motion was approved with the following voting results, by roll call vote: Voting Yea: Councilwoman Atkins, Vice-Mayor Johnson, Councilwoman Pattison. B. RE: ST. MARY THE MOTHER OF GOD FALL FESTIVAL STREET CLOSURE REQUEST Vice-Mayor Johnson advised that the next agenda item is a Staff Report by Interim Town Manager Chris Slemp regarding the request of John Baxley, Office Manager of St. Mary's Catholic Church, to close Fifth Street, between Main and Monroe Streets, on Saturday, September 26, 2026, from 6:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., for the St. Mary the Mother of God Fall Festival. Interim Town Manager Slemp stated that the Safety and Events Committee met regarding this request, and that they would recommend that it be approved. He noted that it is a minimal street closure with minimal disruption. Vice-Mayor Johnson inquired if there was a motion to approve the request of John Baxley, Office Manager of St. Mary's Catholic Church, to close Fifth Street, between Main and Monroe Streets, on Saturday, September 26, 2026, from 6:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., for the St. Mary the Mother of God Fall Festival. Motion made by Councilwoman Atkins, Seconded by Councilwoman Pattison. ViceMayor Johnson inquired if there was any discussion on the motion. There being none, the motion was approved with the following voting in favor, and there being no opposition: Voting Yea: Vice-Mayor Johnson, Councilwoman Pattison, Councilwoman Atkins. C. RE: REAPPOINTMENT TO THE WYTHEVILLE REDEVELOPMENT AND HOUSING AUTHORITY Vice-Mayor Johnson advised that the next agenda item is a Staff Report by Town Clerk Brandi Jones regarding the reappointment of a member to the Wytheville Redevelopment and Housing Authority. Town Clerk Jones stated that this is just a reappointment, and she noted that it is for a four-year term for Lisa Anderson to the Wytheville Redevelopment and Housing Authority. She commented that Ms. Anderson has agreed to serve on the Housing Authority, again, if so desired by the Council. Vice-Mayor Johnson inquired if there was a motion to reappoint Lisa Anderson to the Wytheville Redevelopment and Housing Authority for a four-year term expiring September 8, 2030. Motion made by Councilwoman Pattison, Seconded by Councilwoman Atkins. ViceMayor Johnson inquired if there was any discussion on the motion. There being none, the motion was approved with the following voting in favor, and there being no 9 Section 7, ItemA. opposition: Voting Yea: Vice-Mayor Johnson, Councilwoman Pattison, Councilwoman Atkins. 11. RE: REPORTS A. RE: STAFF TIME - INTERIM TOWN MANAGER CHRIS SLEMP Vice-Mayor Johnson advised that the next agenda item is Interim Town Manager Staff Time. Interim Town Manager Slemp stated that the 9/11 Memorial Service was recently held at the Wytheville Meeting Center. He noted that he would like to thank all those who came together for this special day. Interim Town Manager Slemp advised that he would like to say how much he appreciates Reverend Cox's work on the program, and that he thinks Reverend Cox deserves a special shout out for all his work and dedication to make the service come together. He continued to express his appreciation for all the hard work that went into the event. B. RE: STAFF TIME - TOWN CLERK BRANDI JONES Vice-Mayor Johnson advised that the next agenda item is Town Clerk - Staff Time. Town Clerk Jones stated that she did not have anything to discuss at this time. C. RE: STAFF TIME - ASSISTANT TOWN MANAGER ELAINE HOLETON Vice-Mayor Johnson advised that the next agenda item is Assistant Town Manager Staff Time. She stated that Assistant Town Manager Holeton was not present for this meeting, therefore, she would proceed with the agenda. D. RE: COUNCIL MEMBER TIME Vice-Mayor Johnson advised that the next agenda item is Council Member Time. She inquired if Councilwoman Pattison had anything that she would like to discuss during Council Member Time. Councilwoman Pattison stated that she did not have anything to discuss at this time. Vice-Mayor Johnson inquired if Councilwoman Atkins had anything that she would like to discuss during Council Member Time. Councilwoman Atkins stated the following: "I think Mr. Slemp looked at my notes. Actually, I was going to say it was a tremendous job that everyone did and had taken part in the 9/11 Memorial Ceremony. The people who served on the committee, everyone that attended, all the first responders back 25 years ago, and also the first responders still interactive now in help in our community. I also want to thank the Meeting Center for all the work behind the scenes, such as setup, take down, and also the programs. Awesome
